intentAndPurpose.intent: Render a semantic or custom icon with configurable size, colour role, and emphasis level.

requires: icon prop (semantic name or React element)

rules.name: high emphasis
useWhen: primary content icon requiring strongest contrast

props.description: Icon to display — semantic name, pack id, component, or React element

props.name: appearance
props.description: Colour role. - Omit: inherit the slot parent's role (Badge, Button, Chip…), else `'secondary'`. An ambient `<Surface>` is NOT consulted. - `'auto'`: as above, but fall back to the nearest Surface's role before `'secondary'`. - A role: pin it, ignoring both.

props.name: aria-hidden
props.description: Whether icon is hidden from assistive technology. Default: true when no label

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible label — if provided, icon is not decorative

props.name: customSizeToken
props.description: Dimension token name when `size="custom"` (e.g. `'Spacing-12'`). Sets `--Icon-size: var(--Spacing-12)` on the root. Figma: custom via any dimension token.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: QA / Playwright hook — forwarded to the root span

props.name: size
props.description: Size preset. Default: `'m'` (20px). T-shirt aliases (`2xs`…`2xl`) map to spacing tokens; `custom` uses `--Icon-size`.

interactionBehavior.summary: Icon is a decorative `<span>` with no hover, press, focus, or keyboard behaviour. It is `aria-hidden` unless you pass `aria-label` (which then sets `role="img"`). It does not take focus, does not set a cursor, and does not have a `disabled` or `onPress` prop. For a tappable glyph use `IconButton` (or a `Button` with an `icon` slot) — wrapping this span yourself is how you add interactivity, and that wrapper owns hover / press / focus.
